cues.zh: 整个这一片上界区域——那些至少和 NP 完全问题一样难的问题——被称为“NP-hard”。
cues.en: This whole upper area of problems that are at least as hard as NP-complete is called is called "NP-hard".

cues.zh: 还有“Co-NP”，它指的是这样一类问题：正确答案不容易验证，
cues.en: There's also "Co-NP" -- the class of problems where instead of being easy to check right answers,

cues.zh: 但错误答案很容易排除；它和 NP 是否相同，目前还不确定。
cues.en: it's easy to exclude wrong answers, which may or may not be the same of NP.

cues.zh: 还有“P-SPACE”，它指的是这样一类问题：给定无限的时间就能解决，
cues.en: And then there's "P-SPACE", the class of problems that can be solved given unlimited time,

cues.zh: 但只需要使用多项式量级的内存空间。
cues.en: but using only a polynomial amount of space for memory.

cues.zh: 还有一些问题可以通过概率算法在多项式时间内解决。
cues.en: There are also problems that can be solved probabilistically in polynomial time.

cues.zh: 这类问题称为“BPP”，它和 P 是否相同，目前还不确定。
cues.en: That class is called "BPP", and it may or may not actually be the same as P.

cues.zh: 而 BPP 还有一个量子计算版本，叫作 BQP。
cues.en: And then there's a quantum computing analog of BPP called BQP.

cues.zh: 这里到处都是一些复杂的小类，要解释清楚得花不少功夫，
cues.en: All over the place in here there are complicated little classes that would take a lot of explaining,

cues.zh: 实际上，其中一些最终会被证明是无限的问题层级，每一层都比下面的稍微难一些，
cues.en: and, actually some of these turn out to be infinite hierarchies of problems that are slightly more difficult

cues.zh: 比它们下面的层级更难。
cues.en: from the ones beneath them.

cues.zh: 我们知道存在一个指数层级，可能还有一个多项式层级。
cues.en: We know there's an exponential hierarchy and there's probably a polynomial hierarchy.

cues.zh: 而在这一切之外，是那些任何计算机在任何时间和空间内都无法解决的问题。
cues.en: And out beyond all of this are problems that are, just not solvable by any computer in any amount of time or space.

cues.zh: 对我来说，整个复杂性动物园令人惊叹之处在于，我们实际上在讨论
cues.en: To me, the amazing thing about this whole complexity zoo is that we're talking literally about

cues.zh: 在给定空间和时间下能计算什么。
cues.en: what can be computed in a given amount of space, and time.

cues.zh: 我们在这里不仅是在看计算的本质，
cues.en: We're not just looking at the nature of computation here,

cues.zh: 我们是在看空间和时间本身的本质。
cues.en: we're looking at the nature of space and time themselves.

cues.zh: 这一堆计算复杂性类，我认为最终对
cues.en: This mess of computational complexity classes, I think, ultimately has implications for

cues.zh: 物理学、生物学，以及我们对一切的基本理解都有影响。
cues.en: physics and biology and, for our basic understanding of everything.

cues.zh: 作为这些影响的一个例子，以下是 MIT 复杂性研究员 Scott Aaronson
cues.en: As an example of those implications, here's how Scott Aaronson, a complexity researcher at MIT,

cues.zh: 对 P vs. NP 的直觉解释：
cues.en: explains his intuition about P vs. NP:

cues.zh: “如果 P 等于 NP，那么世界将与我们通常假设的截然不同。
cues.en: "If P were equal to NP, then the world would be a profoundly different place than we usually assume it to be.

cues.zh: “创造性飞跃”并没有什么特殊的价值，
cues.en: There would be no special value in "creative leaps",

cues.zh: 在解决问题和认出已找到的解决方案之间，并不存在根本性的鸿沟。
cues.en: no fundamental gap between solving a problem and recognizing the solution once it's found.

cues.zh: 每个能欣赏交响乐的人都会是莫扎特；
cues.en: Everyone who could appreciate a symphony would be Mozart;

cues.zh: 每个能跟上一步步论证的人都会是高斯。”
cues.en: Everyone who could follow a set-by-step argument would be Gauss."

cues.zh: 我们周围的世界，生命与思想、艺术与天才的本质，
cues.en: The world around us, the nature of living things and ideas, of art and genius,

cues.zh: 都是围绕计算的深层结构塑造的。
cues.en: is molded around the deep structure of computation.

cues.zh: 以一种非常真实的方式，P vs. NP 的某种关联出现在科学家和艺术家的挣扎之中。
cues.en: In a very real way, something connected to P vs. NP shows up in the struggles of scientists and artists.

cues.zh: 肖邦曾说：“简单是最终的成就。
cues.en: Chopin once said: "Simplicity is the final achievement.

cues.zh: 在弹奏了海量的音符之后，浮现出来的正是简单，
cues.en: After one has played a vast quantity of notes and more notes, it is simplicity that emerges

cues.zh: 作为艺术至高无上的奖赏。”
cues.en: as the crowning reward of art."

cues.zh: 杰克·凯鲁亚克是这样说的：“有一天我会找到合适的词，而它们将是简单的。”
cues.en: And Jack Kerouac put it like this: "One day I will find the right words, and they will be simple".
